title: Closing remarks and military service
summary: Russell wraps up; Oxley mentions circuses and army service in Europe and the Pacific; the tape note says he had to play Preservation Hall.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: I didn't remember. I got caught out tonight.

Yeah, I guess we better be finishing up. If there's anything you can think of and real important about your life, I guess you've covered most of it as far as your show work and your early days. That's the main thing we were wondering about because we're trying to study that old history and you might say preserve it so it won't be forgotten. Anything else that you can think of real quickly that you might have left out that you'd want to put on here?

Well, I'll tell you, I would have to think. There's a lot of things, I mean, like different circuses and so forth like that. I mean, like different things I could talk about. I'll tell you what I said, but it takes you time to think. Yeah, I know, that's right. You were with circuses then too.
I was with everything that you could mention.
I had a little music. That's right. I even had ten pieces in the service when I was in there.
Oh, really? In an army. Where was that? Over in France.
Over in France. I was in both theaters. Over in France, Germany, Belgium, Luxembourg, and down in the Pacific, Okinawa, Korea, Japan, Panama.

We were traveling all over again. That's right. Well, I think we better, it won't be late setting up your drums. I'll turn it off. Yeah. This interview ended after about one and a half reels since Dave Oxley had to play next door at Preservation Hall the night of January the 6th. So the balance of this reel will conclude the interview of James Sing Miller, his interview of December 11th, 1964.
